Lumiere Research Scholar Program

Lumiere Education
Paid / aid available

THE OPPORTUNITY

About Lumiere

Turn curiosity into original research.

Lumiere Education connects ambitious high school students with PhD mentors for independent research. Instead of entering an existing lab assignment, a student develops a question in a chosen field and works through a guided research process with one-to-one support.

The project moves from reading and research design to analysis, writing and a final paper. Topics can span science, technology, social sciences or the humanities. Longer tracks include additional support for students who want to pursue publication, while the core value is learning how to think and work like a researcher.

The program is delivered remotely, which makes mentorship possible for students without nearby university research access. It is tuition-based, with financial aid offered by Lumiere. Program length and costs vary by track, so families should check the current official program details before applying.

INSIDE THE EXPERIENCE

What you’ll explore

⌕Find a question

Choose a topic worth investigating and narrow it into an achievable research project.

◉Meet a PhD mentor

Work individually with a researcher who guides reading, methods and critical thinking.

✎Write a paper

Turn findings into a coherent independent paper with an academic structure.

↗Explore publication

Longer tracks can add guidance for submitting work to a student or academic journal.

THE JOURNEY

How it came to life

2020A research mentorship model begins

Lumiere says it was founded by Harvard and Oxford researchers to help high school students work one-to-one with PhD mentors.

NowA wider research community

Lumiere reports more than 7,200 students mentored since 2020 and student work published in more than 50 academic journals. These are Lumiere-wide figures, not Relay outcomes.

READY TO BEGIN?

Your next steps

  1. Choose the research field and track that match your interests and available time.
  2. Check the current cohort deadline, tuition and aid information on Lumiere's site.
  3. Prepare to discuss the question you want to investigate and the skills you hope to build.
